question: C's next neighbour is D. What should happen?
context: We are exploring from C, at distance 1. D was already discovered from B, with distance 2.

choices.label: Skip D: its distance is already final
choices.feedback: Right. A route through C would also reach D in 2 streets. BFS gives every corner its smallest distance the first time it is discovered, so D is skipped.

choices.label: Add D to the queue again
choices.feedback: That would explore D twice, and on larger maps the repeats add up fast. A discovered corner already has its final distance, so it is skipped.

choices.label: Record D as reached from C instead
choices.feedback: Both routes to D are 2 streets long, so nothing improves. BFS keeps the first discovery and moves on.
